resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (CO) for resale
resale_co.lead_time: Submit everything before the inspection can be scheduled; inspections are only on Thursdays, 9 AM to 12 PM. Do not schedule settlement until all items are submitted and approved.
requirements: Handrails on stairs with 2 or more steps
Hot water relief valve extension 6 inches from the floor; appliances vented properly
Emergency exit if there is sleeping on a 3rd floor
Windows, screens, and interior and exterior doors in good condition
Working heating system, plumbing and water pressure; GFCI outlets near water
Ceilings, walls, floors and interior and exterior paint in good condition; sound roof
Extermination, general clean up inside and out, and a garbage container

House number on the front of the house and a white 911 numbering post by the street (6 ft 4x4 post, 4 ft above ground, black numbers at least 4 inches or 3 inches if reflective, on both sides, near the driveway)

fees.label: CO inspection fee (check payable to Downe Township)
fees.quote: $25 CHECK for Inspection Fee - (Please make the check out to Downe Township.)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Before the inspection is scheduled, send to Downe Township, Attn: Zoning, 288 Main Street, Newport NJ 08345: (1) a septic certificate or septic waiver in the buyers' name, (2) a water certificate (Fortescue properties with public water are exempt), both from the Cumberland County Health Department, 309 Buck Street, Millville (856-327-7602), (3) the fire certificate from the City of Bridgeton Fire Department, (4) a $25 check payable to Downe Township and (5) the Certificate of Occupancy Application. The Zoning Office then calls to schedule the Thursday morning inspection. Buyers cannot move in until the CO is approved.

resale_co.notes: Downe Township requires a Certificate of Occupancy for resales and long-term rentals, run by the Zoning Officer. The Township's CO information sheet (effective January 1, 2026; scanned PDF posted July 2026, read visually) lists what must be submitted before the inspection is scheduled, including the Bridgeton fire certificate. The Zoning Office email is hidden by email protection on the Township web pages; it was decoded from the page and matches the address printed on the CO sheet. Ordinance 2021-10 lets a Cumberland County Health Department septic waiver satisfy the septic requirement for the Township CO. Tony Loteck is the Code Enforcement officer (856-447-3100 x102 on the staff directory). The CO form is also used for long-term rentals; short-term rentals have a separate ordinance (2024-05).

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.lead_time: Submit the request 2 to 3 weeks before settlement; the lowest fee applies when the request is received 10 or more business days before settlement.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Downe Township as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: Downe Township's fire code is enforced by the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention under a shared services agreement (effective January 2021; Township Ordinance 2025-14, adopted December 8, 2025, says the Bridgeton Bureau issues the smoke/CO certificates and the fee follows the current City of Bridgeton ordinance). The Bridgeton online application lists Downe Township as a choice, and the fees, lead time and 90-day validity come from the Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025). The Township's CO sheet gives 856-451-0090 for fire certificate questions; the Bureau's page gives (856) 451-0091. No fire extinguisher is listed on the current Bridgeton guideline sheet (P.L.2025, c.19).
